endorsements.quote: To ensure demographic representation in datasets, it is necessary to implement policies that require mandatory representation criteria for approval and adoption.

Most studies did not evaluate the algorithm’s performance across different demographic groups or use ca libration and fairness (e.g., demographic parity, equal opportunity) metrics to assess disparities in predictions across these groups12,13.

unlisted_practices: Conduct external validation of AI models to ensure they generalize beyond the datasets used for training.
Use the QUADAS-AI framework to evaluate AI diagnostic models for risk of bias and applicability.
Develop universal, standardized evaluation protocols for AI models to mitigate the propagation of health inequities.
Organize and structure health data for compatibility and interoperability to enable development of multimodal algorithms.
Address data quality and bias problems before rapid, large-scale adoption of AI in healthcare.
Enforce bias testing of AI tools.
Foster collaboration among clinicians, researchers, policymakers, and entrepreneurs in developing AI tools for diabetes care.

screen.reason: This is a commentary/editorial discussing findings of a scoping review on AI for diabetes risk prediction and emphasizing implementation challenges, bias, external validation, and recommendations for equitable deployment.
